walkthrough: Day 1, 0-2 min: page loads. I press H and land on one heading for the thread, then the text box. Typing the problem is easy. Whether the reply gets read out depends on the log having aria-live=polite. If it doesn't, I'm pressing Shift+Tab and arrowing up after every send to find out whether it answered.
2-12 min: one question at a time works well for me because it's linear and there's no layout to learn. I type 'on-time delivery fell from 94% to 86%' and answer 6-8 follow-ups.

12-15 min: the 'what we understood' summary arrives as a message. I read it line by line in browse mode and confirm. It's fine if it's a real list and the buttons have names like 'Confirm understanding', not just 'Confirm'.

15-30 min: data items come in as separate messages. Each one has Upload, Connect and Invite buttons, so the 3rd Upload button I tab to sounds exactly like the 1st. STUCK: I can't tell which data item a button belongs to unless the accessible name includes the item name.
Day 2, 0-3 min: changing the goal is the easiest of the four here. I type 'Manager says the real question is whether to drop carrier X.' That's natural. No form to find.

Day 2, 3-10 min: STUCK. Day 1's summary is still sitting above in the thread. When the consultant posts a new one, which is current? I have to scroll through the log message by message to compare them. I want the old one marked 'replaced' in text.

Day 2, 10-15 min: I type 'what do you still need?' and get a list. Good, that saves me. But are the data items for the old goal still listed? If carrier-level data is needed now, does a new item appear somewhere above me?
Report day: a long message in a chat log. If it has real headings and the source tags are text, I can read it. If it's one big blob inside a listitem, I'll export to Word and read it there.
Possible abandon point: around day 4, when the thread has 80+ messages and I need to get back to one data item.
blockers: FIXABLE: buttons repeated in every message need names that include the item ('Upload shipment log')
FIXABLE: superseded summaries and data items must say 'replaced on day 2' in text
FIXABLE: the new-message live region must announce politely and must not re-read the whole thread
INHERENT: a long linear log has no fixed place for 'current state'. Finding things again later costs me more than it costs a sighted user.
W.quote: Changing my mind is just typing a sentence, that's great. Then I spend ten minutes arrowing through history to work out which version of 'what we understood' is the live one.

walkthrough: Day 1, 0-10 min: same as W for the chat stage, and fine.

10-11 min: STUCK. The consultant 'creates the engagement page' and the chat moves to a side panel. What happens to my focus? If it stays in the chat input I don't know a page appeared. If it jumps to the page I've lost my place mid-conversation. Either way I need a spoken message: 'Engagement page created. Focus moved to Your next step. Chat is now in the side panel, press F6 / landmark to reach it.'
11-20 min: on the page I can navigate by H and landmarks: next step, progress in words, understood, data checklist. This part is good.

20-30 min: I ask in the side panel 'why do you need carrier scan data?' STUCK. Two live areas compete. If the panel reply and a page update both announce, NVDA talks over itself, or one interrupts the other. If only the panel announces, page changes happen silently somewhere I can't see.
Day 2, 0-5 min: I find the side panel (D for landmarks, or a shortcut if one exists) and type the carrier X change. That's natural, as in W.

Day 2, 5-15 min: STUCK, and this is the worst one. 'Answers can turn into page changes.' What changed? Did 'What we understood' get rewritten, and were data items added or removed? A sighted user sees a highlight. I need a text change summary ('3 changes to your page: goal updated, 2 data items added, 1 removed'), with links that move focus there.
Day 2: it then goes to the approver queue because the framing changed. Does the page say 'waiting on consultant to approve new goal' in text? If it does, I'm fine.
Possible abandon point: the first time I get lost bouncing between the panel and the page, or a reply comes in while I'm reading the checklist and NVDA cuts me off mid-sentence.
blockers: FIXABLE but high-risk: focus management at the chat-to-page handover
FIXABLE: one live-region policy (panel replies polite, page changes summarised once, never assertive)
FIXABLE: a keyboard shortcut and landmark to toggle between panel and page, and it must not trap focus
FIXABLE: a text diff of page changes made from chat
INHERENT: two simultaneous surfaces. Sighted users read both at a glance. I can only be in one at a time, so the side panel's 'always there' advantage is mostly lost on me.
Z.quote: Sighted people get a chat next to a page. I get two things talking at once and a page that rearranged itself while I wasn't looking.

walkthrough: Day 1, 0-3 min: one text box, labelled. I type the problem. 3-5 follow-up questions on the same page. If they're normal labelled fields I can tab through them fast, quicker than chat.

3-10 min: I press H to 'Your next step': one action, owner, time. This is exactly what I want and it's always in the same place. The progress tracker in words reads fine if it's a list with 'current step' in text, not colour.

10-15 min: I confirm 'What we understood'. The editable lines worry me. If they're contenteditable or click-to-edit, NVDA browse/focus mode switching gets messy. Real text inputs with an Edit button each are fine.
15-30 min: the data checklist as a list or table works well for me. Each item reads as name, Must have, status, actions.

Day 2, 0-8 min: STUCK. My manager changed the actual question, and that isn't 'edit a line'. I hunt for a 'Change the question' action and find only editable lines. So I rewrite the goal line myself and hope the consultant notices. Maybe I end up emailing them instead.
Day 2, 8-12 min: after the edit, do the data items update? Does 'Your next step' change to 'waiting on consultant to re-confirm'? If the next-step card changes and says so, I trust it.

Report day: the report moves to the top and finished sections collapse. STUCK (mild): my mental map of the page has changed, and H takes me somewhere different than yesterday. Collapsed sections must be buttons with aria-expanded, or they've vanished for me.
No real abandon point. The worst case is that I phone the consultant to change the goal.
blockers: FIXABLE: no explicit 'the question changed' path. Line-editing is the wrong size of action for a goal change.
FIXABLE: editable lines must be standard inputs, not contenteditable
FIXABLE: report moving and sections collapsing must be announced, keep a fixed heading order, and use aria-expanded
INHERENT: none serious. A single page with headings is the pattern my screen reader is built for.
X.quote: Give me one page with headings and a 'next step' I can jump to with H, and I'm happy. Just don't make me rewrite the goal one line at a time as if it were a typo.

walkthrough: Day 1, 0-12 min: a 5-step form. Honestly, a well-labelled form is fine for me, and it's predictable. Each step must announce 'Step 2 of 5', and errors must stay on screen and be linked.

Step 2: 'problem category' dropdown. Logistics on-time delivery might not fit a category, so I pick 'Operations' and hope. 'Goals with suggestions': if the suggestions are clickable chips or toggle styling with no aria-pressed, they're invisible to me. STUCK briefly.
12-25 min: the data page is a table. Good. I'm comfortable with Ctrl+Alt+arrows, and row and column headers matter.

Dashboard: STUCK. The tiles say 'Data completeness 60%' and 'Analysis 30%'. Fine if they're text. The 'early charts' are almost certainly an SVG or canvas with no data table, so they're useless to me. Status tiles often rely on a coloured dot. 'Messages' as a tile means a mini chat buried in a grid.

Day 2, 0-15 min: STUCK, and it's the main one. The intake form was submitted. Where do I change the goal? Do I go back to the draft? Is it locked? Do I use the messages tile? I'd probably write in messages and get no sign that the engagement goal actually changed. The percentages wouldn't move to show it either.
Possible abandon point: here. I'd email the consultant directly and use the platform only for uploads.
Report: viewable as a formal Word/PDF document. That's actually where Y does best for me.
blockers: INHERENT: the form front-loads the goal and treats it as fixed. Changing it is off the designed path.
INHERENT: a dashboard of visual tiles. Percentages and charts are glanceable for sighted users and give me nothing to act on.
FIXABLE: charts need text summaries or a data table
FIXABLE: status must be in text, not colour
FIXABLE: goal suggestions need aria-pressed and checkbox semantics
Y.quote: A dashboard is a picture of progress. I can't see pictures, and 60% complete doesn't tell me what to do next.

change_in_favourite: In X: (1) add a 'Our question has changed' button beside 'What we understood'. It opens one text field, sends to the consultant, and the next-step card then says in text 'Waiting on consultant to re-confirm the new question (expected Wed)'. Afterwards, show a short list of what changed in data items, with old items marked 'no longer needed' instead of silently disappearing. (2) Keep the heading order fixed. Put the report under a stable 'Report' heading and add a skip link at the top instead of moving it, or at least announce 'Report is ready, now the first section'. (3) Use real inputs for the editable lines. (4) Steal W's 'what do you still need?' as a typed question box, so I can ask instead of navigating.
